items: **Volatile storage** is temporary. Values stored in variables are lost when the computer loses power. **RAM** is used when a Java program stores a value in a variable.
**Non-volatile storage** is permanent. A Java program saved on a disk uses non-volatile storage.

blocks.value: **A computer file is a collection of data stored on a non-volatile device.**

items: A **text file** consists of data that can be read in a text editor. Data is encoded using a scheme, most commonly **ASCII** or **Unicode**. Examples: program files, application files.

A **binary file** contains data not encoded as text. Its contents cannot be understood by viewing them in a text editor. Examples: images, music, and the `.class` files created when Java programs are compiled.

blocks.value: Both share the characteristics of **size**, **name**, and **date and time of creation**.
Permanent files are commonly stored in the main or **root** directory. **Folders** or **directories** organize them, and folders may contain folders.
**The complete list of the disk drive plus the hierarchy of directories in which a file is located is called a path.**
In Windows, the **backslash (`\`)** is the **path delimiter**: the special character separating path components.

blocks.title: In Java source, a backslash must be doubled

blocks.value: `\` begins an escape sequence, so a Windows path is written `"C:\\Java\\Chapter8\\example.txt"`. Forward slashes also work on Windows and are more portable: `"C:/Java/Chapter8/example.txt"`.
